finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication

trace.note: route POST /restore, no auth filter or before block
Base64.decode64(params[:state]) yields attacker bytes, which go directly into Marshal.load
state.inspect is called on the deserialized object, which can also trigger gadget methods

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, signature/HMAC, or class allowlist. Marshal.load has no safe mode. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection does not block this POST. The only other route, /import, uses JSON.parse, which is safe, and /health is static.

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load in the unauthenticated POST /restore route (app.rb:5), with no before filter, auth, HMAC or class allowlist anywhere in the single-file app.
